idiom_name: module-load initialisation + a promise created eagerly (work starts at construction)
implementation_notes: The realisation collapses into ES module semantics: a module body and its imports are evaluated once before the importer's body runs, so an init module that opens the client and exports the result is the eager-acquisition structure - and a promise is eager by construction, because the executor runs when the promise is created, not on the first await or then. Use top-level await when consumers must not run before the resource is ready, memoise the started work in a module-level const, and re-create it on failure so one bad boot does not poison every consumer for the process lifetime. Where the platform owns the resource (HTTP connections, module loading), the same decision appears one layer down as preconnect/preload hints and server-side warm-up.
pitfalls: A promise started eagerly that later rejects without a handler is an unhandled rejection - fatal by default on modern Node - so the warm-up needs its own error path.
Module-scope work runs on the single JS thread, so an eagerly decoded model or synchronous warm-up delays every import and blocks the event loop.
Import cycles observe partially initialised modules, so an eagerly acquired binding can be undefined in whichever module the runtime evaluates first.
